Similarly, USGS withholds data for domestic production of primary tellurium-containing residues and primary selenium-containing residues, because only two producing facilities operated during 2024 (U.S. Geological Survey 2025l, 2025n). USGS notes that no tellurium or selenium refining exists in the United States, so all residues are exported for further processing. First Solar has a partnership with 5N Plus to refine tellurium sourced from a Utah facility (Rio Tinto) at the 5N Plus refinery in Canada, which is then reimported within refined CdTe powder into the United States for use in First Solar manufacturing facilities (5N Plus 2022). Rio Tinto is not believed to provide all the tellurium-containing residues 5N Plus processes (Pickerel 2025a); they provide only about 1 GW -equivalent. Thus, 5N Plus likely uses tellurium from other dc locations, which may include China (the leading global producer of tellurium). Some secondary tellurium was recovered from recycled CdTe PV in the United States in 2024. However, quantities are comparatively small, because few CdTe modules have reached their end of life (U.S. Geological Survey 2025n), and some are landfilled (Meagley et al. 2025). First Solar claims its modules are designed so more than 90% of the module material can be recovered for reuse and that the company has 500 MW of recycling capacity (First Solar 2025b). dc 3.4.3 Imports/Exports of CdTe Powder The United States has imported approximately 7 kt of “salts of inorganic acids” (which includes CdTe powder)40 annually in recent years. We estimate First Solar required approximately 0.5 kt of refined CdTe powder to produce the 6.3 GW of modules it made domestically in 2024. The dc average customs value of these imports was approximately $3/kg in 2024, which is much lower than the estimated price for refined CdTe powder discussed in the following section. For these reasons, we conclude that large volumes of less expensive compounds are reported under this code, obscuring insights that could be drawn about CdTe powder exclusively (though some of the discrepancy could be explained by stockpiling refined CdTe powder for future use). 5N Plus (a supplier of CdTe powder to First Solar) has production locations in Canada and Germany. The company announced a 50% increase in its supply contract with First Solar during 2024 (5N Plus 2024), reaching 3 times the size of its contract in 2022 (Willing 2025). In early 2025, China placed export controls on tellurium and compounds such as CdTe and CdZnTe, forcing exporters to obtain special approval from China’s Ministry of Commerce and General Administration of customs (V. Shaw 2025a). 3.4.4 Regional Pricing for CdTe Powder This section reports on constituent metal pricing, because direct pricing information for CdTe powder is not readily available.
